children: Welspun Corp shares gained up to 5 percent in Monday's trading session after its associate company East Pipes Integrated Company for Industry (EPIC) won a contract from Saudi Arabian Oil Co. (Aramco) for manufacturing and supply of steel pipes worth over Rs 2,000 crore.

Shares of Welspun Corp hit an intraday high of Rs 2,797.60 per share on the NSE, rising more than 5 percent. However, profit booking at higher levels pulled the stock down, and it was quoting at Rs 2,721.40, up 2.3 percent, around 11:50 a.m.

In an exchange filing, Welspun Corp said EPIC, a listed entity in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, announced on the Saudi Stock Exchange the signing of a contract with Aramco for manufacturing and supply of steel pipes for a total value exceeding 771 million Saudi riyals (approximately Rs 2,000 crore), including value-added tax.
The duration of the contract is six months, and its financial impact will be reflected from the fourth quarter of FY2026-27 through the first quarter of FY2027-28, the company said.
EPIC is Saudi Arabia's leading manufacturer of Helical Submerged Arc Welded (HSAW) pipes, according to the filing.
The company has fully integrated manufacturing facilities and a track record of executing large orders in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, it said.
Shares of the company are up 240.58 percent in 2026 so far, according to the data available on BSE Analytics.
